name: Protein
whatIsIt: A macronutrient made of amino acids that the body uses as a building material.
whyNeeded: Supports the growth and repair of muscles, skin, and other tissues, and is used to make enzymes and hormones.
generalNote: Adults commonly reference roughly 0.8g per kg of body weight per day as a general baseline; needs vary by age, activity, and individual circumstances.

name: Carbohydrates
whatIsIt: The body's primary energy source, found in grains, fruits, vegetables, and legumes.
whyNeeded: Fuels daily activity and brain function; whole-food sources also bring fiber and micronutrients along with the energy.
generalNote: Whole grains, fruits, and legumes are commonly favored over refined/added-sugar sources for the same amount of carbohydrate.

name: Fat
whatIsIt: A concentrated energy source that also helps the body absorb certain vitamins.
whyNeeded: Needed for hormone production, cell structure, and absorbing fat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K.
generalNote: Sources like nuts, seeds, and dairy provide fat along with other nutrients, unlike isolated oils or fried foods.

name: Fiber
whatIsIt: The part of plant food the body doesn't fully digest.
whyNeeded: Supports digestion and regularity, and helps with a feeling of fullness after meals.
generalNote: Legumes, whole grains, fruits, and vegetables are the most reliable everyday sources.

name: Calcium
whatIsIt: A mineral stored mainly in bones and teeth.
whyNeeded: Supports bone and teeth structure, and plays a role in muscle and nerve function.
generalNote: Dairy foods, ragi, and fortified plant milks are commonly relied-on everyday sources.

name: Iron
whatIsIt: A mineral that is part of hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen.
whyNeeded: Needed for oxygen transport in the blood and everyday energy levels.
generalNote: Pairing iron-containing plant foods with a source of vitamin C can help the body absorb the iron.

name: Potassium
whatIsIt: A mineral that helps balance fluids in the body.
whyNeeded: Supports normal muscle and nerve function, and helps balance the effects of sodium.
generalNote: Fruits, vegetables, and legumes are the main everyday sources.

name: Magnesium
whatIsIt: A mineral involved in hundreds of chemical reactions in the body.
whyNeeded: Supports muscle and nerve function, and energy production.
generalNote: Leafy greens, nuts, and whole grains are commonly relied-on sources.

name: Zinc
whatIsIt: A trace mineral needed in small amounts.
whyNeeded: Supports immune function and wound healing.
generalNote: Legumes, dairy, nuts, and meat/poultry are common everyday sources.

name: Vitamin A
whyNeeded: Supports vision, skin, and immune function.
generalNote: Leafy greens and dairy are common everyday sources.

name: Vitamin C
whyNeeded: Supports immune function, skin health, and helps the body absorb iron from plant foods.
generalNote: Fruits and vegetables are the main everyday sources; this vitamin is sensitive to prolonged cooking.

name: Vitamin D
whatIsIt: A fat-soluble vitamin the body can also make from sunlight exposure.
whyNeeded: Supports calcium absorption and bone health.
generalNote: Fortified milk and moderate sunlight exposure are common everyday sources.

name: Vitamin B12
whatIsIt: A vitamin found mainly in animal foods and fortified products.
whyNeeded: Supports nerve function and the formation of red blood cells.
generalNote: People eating little or no animal products often rely on fortified foods for this nutrient.

name: Sodium
whatIsIt: A mineral found naturally in food and added heavily during processing and cooking.
whyNeeded: Needed in small amounts for fluid balance and nerve function, but commonly consumed in excess.
generalNote: Processed, packaged, and restaurant foods are the biggest everyday contributors — often more than salt added at home.

name: Added sugar
whatIsIt: Sugar added to food during processing or preparation, separate from sugars naturally present in fruit or milk.
whyNeeded: Not required by the body; commonly tracked to help limit intake rather than to ensure adequacy.
generalNote: Sweetened beverages, desserts, and packaged snacks are the most common everyday sources.
